coverage_summary: Reviewed all five trajectories, including modality preprocessing, fusion, pretraining branches, and downstream task heads. Several blocking unsupported bindings and decompositions require revision.

findings.detail: The graph asserts selection of informative regions from the whole WSI, but the paper only assumes/decomposes already informative regions and gives no detection or selection operation.

evidence.quote: we decompose the informative regions of each WSI into a set of non-overlapping 256 × 256 pixels patches

findings.required_change: Represent informative regions as a source-defined boundary or opaque preprocessing result; remove the asserted select call from wsi to wsi_informative_regions.

findings.detail: Expert-output concatenation is bound as a self-loop: expert_concat_Zdoubleprime is both its input and output, while the preceding opaque expert step already returns the concatenated result.

evidence.quote: Z ′′ ← concat ( { z h ′′ , z g ′′ , z t ′′ } )

findings.required_change: Either expose the available per-modality expert outputs and concatenate them here, or remove this duplicate call and retain concatenation inside the opaque expert boundary.

findings.detail: Random MLM selection is over h, g, and t, while each branch is separately conditioned on modality availability. The graph therefore has no documented behavior when the selected modality is absent, despite asserting one valid selected loss.

evidence.quote: Input: Dataset D = { ( x h , x g , x t ) } with optional WSI ( x h ), omics ( x g ), and reports ( x t )
c ← Random ( h, g, t ) // Random choose one modality to perform MLM

findings.required_change: Represent the unavailable-modality case explicitly and leave its handling unresolved; do not assert that exactly one available MLM branch is selected unless the paper establishes that rule.

findings.detail: The WSI MLM objective receives only masked regions and labels, but the algorithm explicitly defines the MLM objective on F. The graph omits the documented fused/model representation input and does not preserve the unspecified prediction-target receipt.

evidence.quote: L MLM ← MLM c ( F ) // Modality-specific MLM of the chosen modality c
We randomly select some regions to mask and use the mean of the original features within the regions as labels.

findings.required_change: Bind the objective to the documented F representation and retain the target/prediction-head interface as unresolved rather than using only the masked-region operands.

findings.detail: The omics MLM objective omits the documented F input and has no explicit target receipt. Its current inputs are only masked expression values and pathway context.

evidence.quote: L MLM ← MLM c ( F ) // Modality-specific MLM of the chosen modality c
For omics, we randomly mask a certain proportion of gene expression values in each pathway.

findings.required_change: Bind the objective to F or preserve that model-output boundary, and represent the omics targets and prediction head as unspecified rather than omitting the documented objective input.

findings.detail: The report MLM objective omits the documented F input and does not preserve the target receipt implied by the MLM objective.

evidence.quote: L MLM ← MLM c ( F ) // Modality-specific MLM of the chosen modality c
For reports, we adopt the original MLM approach.

findings.required_change: Bind the objective to the documented model representation and retain the original MLM target/prediction interface as unresolved.

findings.detail: The graph invents a computation of all three candidate MLM losses followed by select. The paper specifies a chosen-modality objective MLM_c(F), not this order or candidate-loss materialization.

evidence.quote: c ← Random ( h, g, t ) // Random choose one modality to perform MLM
L MLM ← MLM c ( F ) // Modality-specific MLM of the chosen modality c

findings.required_change: Replace the candidate-loss select chain with a conditional selected-modality MLM boundary, preserving unavailable-modality behavior as unknown.

findings.detail: The CLIP aggregation asserts that only available pairwise terms contribute. The paper gives a three-term sum and an algorithmic CLIP call, but does not establish missing-modality aggregation semantics.

evidence.quote: Finally, we can get L CLIP such as L CLIP = L H -G + L G -T + L T -H .
L CLIP ← CLIP ( F h , F g , F t )

findings.required_change: Remove the asserted available-pair omission rule and retain missing-modality CLIP handling as an opaque or unresolved boundary.

findings.detail: The WSI subtyping path decomposes the task into an MLP feature head followed by a separate classifier, but the paper only states that task heads have no architectural constraints and that non-multimodal tasks use MLPs.

evidence.quote: we do not impose any architectural constraints on the task heads. For multimodal tasks, we employ cross-attention to re-embed the CLS tokens, while for other tasks, we use MLPs.

findings.required_change: Use one opaque MLP/task-head boundary from the documented WSI representation to subtype predictions, unless the paper establishes a separate classifier stage.

findings.detail: The subtype CE objective has no ground-truth label input, although the paper explicitly defines CE using an associated label and one-hot ground truth.

evidence.quote: Let a WSI be denoted by X with an associated slide-level label y
where y c is the one-hot encoded ground-truth label for class c

findings.required_change: Add the subtype ground-truth label as an objective input, keeping encoding and reduction details unspecified.

findings.detail: The mutation-prediction path makes the same unsupported two-stage decomposition: MLP task features followed by a separate classifier.

evidence.quote: we do not impose any architectural constraints on the task heads. For multimodal tasks, we employ cross-attention to re-embed the CLS tokens, while for other tasks, we use MLPs.

findings.required_change: Use one opaque MLP/task-head boundary to mutation predictions, unless a separate classifier is documented.

findings.detail: The mutation CE objective omits the mutation ground-truth labels required by the paper's CE formulation.

evidence.quote: Let a WSI be denoted by X with an associated slide-level label y
where y c is the one-hot encoded ground-truth label for class c

findings.required_change: Add TP53/EGFR mutation labels as objective inputs, without asserting their serialization or head sharing.

findings.detail: The report-generation cross-attention call consumes the full WSI fusion sequence, while the paper only documents cross-attention for re-embedding CLS tokens. The separate conditioning-to-decoder order is also not established.

evidence.quote: For multimodal tasks, we employ cross-attention to re-embed the CLS tokens, while for other tasks, we use MLPs.
(4) Report generation ( h. → t. ).

findings.required_change: Bind the documented cross-attention boundary to an explicitly identified CLS representation, or retain the entire report-generation head as opaque with its query/key/value and decoder interface unresolved.

findings.detail: The report-generation CE objective receives only generated tokens and omits the target report/caption sequence required for supervised CE training.

evidence.quote: The dataset was constructed by extracting diagnostic captions from pathology reports corresponding to stomach adenocarcinoma endoscopic biopsy specimens and pairing them with image patches
where y c is the one-hot encoded ground-truth label for class c

findings.required_change: Add the target report-token sequence as an objective input, leaving tokenization, teacher forcing, and reduction unspecified.

findings.detail: The Cox loss step receives only risk scores, but the paper defines censoring indicators, event times, and risk sets as part of the Cox objective.

evidence.quote: Each patient sample includes: (1) a censorship indicator c ∈ 0 , 1 ... and (2) a time-to-event value t i .
where U denotes the set of uncensored patients, and R i is the risk set for patient i

findings.required_change: Add event/censoring and time/risk-set supervision inputs, while leaving the exact implementation unresolved.
